transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I'm here because I've been struggling with episodes where I eat really large amounts of food. It feels like I lose all control and just can't stop myself once I start.

After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? This will help me understand what kind of eating problem you’re dealing with.
No, I don't do anything like that to try to make up for the food. I've never forced myself to throw up, used laxatives, or tried to fast or over-exercise afterward.
How often do these episodes happen, and for about how many months have they been going on?
They happen at least once a week on average, sometimes even more than that. This pattern has been going on for about a year now.

During these episodes, do you also tend to eat much more quickly than usual, eat until you feel uncomfortably full, eat when you’re not physically hungry, eat alone because you feel embarrassed, or feel disgusted, depressed, or guilty afterward?

Yes, I definitely eat much faster than normal during these episodes and keep going until I'm uncomfortably full. Afterwards, I always feel terrible—just completely disgusted with myself, depressed, and guilty. I'm not really sure if I do it when I'm not hungry or if I eat alone out of embarrassment, though.
Is your self-esteem or how you feel about yourself mainly shaped by your body weight or body shape?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about my self-esteem in that way or how much my weight or shape affects it.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about your weight or body shape, or feel that they strongly affect how good or bad you feel about yourself?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't think I spend much time worrying about my weight or shape in that way. My focus and distress are really just about the eating episodes themselves and how out of control they feel.
